_comment: COMMITTED alias map for normalise-entities.py. Every entry is a HUMAN decision, carries a reason and names the source it was taken from. NOTHING HERE IS DERIVED and no tool ever writes to this file: an agent that wants a new merge edits this file, states why, and commits it. Fuzzy similarity is NEVER a reason - two different people with similar names (Titus vs Jacob Burckhardt, Seyyed Hossein Nasr vs David Nasser) stay separate, and the pairs a similarity check would propose are listed under doNotMerge so they are not re-litigated every run. Merges that need no entry here: forms differing only by diacritics, punctuation, case or whitespace are folded mechanically by the tool ('Rene Guenon' == 'Rene Guenon' == 'Rene Guenon'), so listing them here is redundant and the tool says so.
_scope: The COF manifest's `entities` field, which ranks runs of CAPITALISED TOKENS - i.e. multiword proper nouns. Single-token manglings recorded in the projects' KEYWORDS.md (`Genon`, `Ganon`, `Chuon`, `Comarassoume`, `Lefebre`) can never appear in that field and are deliberately absent here; they are full-text search traps and live in the projects' KEYWORDS.md. Variants listed here but never seen in the manifest are reported as `unused` on every run rather than silently kept.
_evidence: An `evidence` entry is (aula, quote). The quote is checked as a LITERAL substring of that aula's file on every run; a quote that no longer verifies is reported as an error. Quotation is sparing and attributed to a specific aula, per archive/NOTICE.md and adr/0005-corpus-admission.md.

aliases.reason: ASR of the scholastic's name. The corpus never writes 'Scotus'; the transcriptions render it as an English surname. The five aulas carrying 'John Don Scott' put it in scholastic company - COF389 attributes to him the doctrine of individuating difference ('exceidade' = haecceitas) in an explicit dispute with Aquinas. 'Dan Scott' (COF327) is deliberately NOT included: it sits in the same aula as 'John Don Scott' and could be a second mangling or a different name, and that is a human call, not this tool's.
aliases.source: hand-checked against the corpus while building this map (2026-07-25); the ASR-mangling discipline is perennialism/KEYWORDS.md, 'ASR manglings observed in the vaulted transcripts'

evidence.quote: John Don Scott chamado a sua exceidade

aliases.reason: Truncation of an ASR form: the transcriptions render 'Ortega y Gasset' as 'Ortega Cela' and, more often, cut it to 'Ortega C'. COF528 names the book in the same sentence ('a Rebellao de Las Massas' = La rebelion de las masas, Ortega y Gasset 1929). The unmangled 'Ortega Y Gasset' occurs in exactly one aula, the truncation in five - merging is the difference between finding one lecture and finding six.
aliases.source: hand-checked against the corpus while building this map (2026-07-25)

evidence.quote: José Ortega Cela, a Rebellão de Las Massas
A presença do Ortega C ali já era estranha

aliases.reason: Recorded ASR manglings of Lings: the final -s is dropped, and 'Martin Lynch' was observed in COF. 'Martin Lins' is NOT merged - see doNotMerge; it may well be the same name but no hand measurement records it, and a guess is not a merge.
aliases.source: perennialism/KEYWORDS.md - 'Lings -> Martin Ling (singular), Martin Lynch (COF)'; tariqa/KEYWORDS.md ASR table - 'Martin Lings | Martin links, Martins'

aliases.reason: Multiword ASR forms of the name recorded in the traps tables. The unaccented and mixed-accent forms the corpus actually uses ('Rene Guenon', 'Rene Guenon', 'Rene Guenon') need no entry: they fold together mechanically.
aliases.source: perennialism/KEYWORDS.md - 'Guénon -> ... rune genon (transcript-48) ... Renê guon (transcript-43) ... Rene ganon, Rene Ganon (transcript-56), Renê ganon (transcript-51)'

aliases.reason: Every element of the name is mangled by ASR and the surname collides with Gamal Abdel Nasser; the traps tables record these three multiword forms. The collision is why the map is explicit: see doNotMerge for 'David Nasser', a different person present in this same index.
aliases.source: tariqa/KEYWORDS.md ASR table - 'Seyyed Hossein Nasr | NASA, said Hussain nasser'; perennialism/KEYWORDS.md - 'transcript-66 renders him seed jossei Nasser and seed hosi Nasser in consecutive lines'

aliases.reason: Recorded ASR forms, including the Portuguese-first-name re-cuts seen in COF. Merging on the SURNAME alone would be wrong here in both directions: Jacob Burckhardt (COF, correctly spelled) is the Swiss historian, and 'Burke' in the fsspx transcripts is Cardinal Raymond Burke.
aliases.source: perennialism/KEYWORDS.md - 'Burckhardt -> Burkart, Burkhart, Burkhan, Burkard, Burkle, Burkher, Tito Zumbur, Tito Bucke (COF)'; tariqa/KEYWORDS.md ASR table - 'Titus Burckhardt | Titus burkhard, Burkhart'

aliases.reason: Multiword ASR forms of Coomaraswamy recorded in the vault. The single-token COF forms ('Comarassoume', 'Comarassame', 'Comarassome', 'Comarassuame', 'Comarassao') are out of scope for an index of multiword runs - see _scope. Rama P. Coomaraswamy (his son, a figure in fsspx and tariqa) is a different person and is not merged.
aliases.source: tariqa/KEYWORDS.md ASR section - 'Coomaraswamy - Kumarazuami (9), Comaram (5) ... anandakumara Swami (transcript-121, transcript-57) ... com Marazvam'

doNotMerge.reason: Two different men who share a surname: the perennialist author (d. 1984) and the Swiss cultural historian (d. 1897). Both are in the corpus, correctly spelled, in different aulas.
doNotMerge.source: perennialism/KEYWORDS.md figures[6] vs the corpus's own 'Jacob Burckhardt'

doNotMerge.reason: David Nasser is a Brazilian journalist; the surname collision with Nasr/Nasser is exactly the trap the traps table warns about.
doNotMerge.source: perennialism/KEYWORDS.md - 'the surname collides with Gamal Abdel Nasser ... never by Nasr alone'

doNotMerge.reason: Left open on purpose. 'Martin Lins' may be a further mangling of Lings, but no hand measurement records it, and Álvaro Lins is a Brazilian critic the corpus discusses - so the surname is live in this corpus on its own account. A human decides; the tool reports it as a suggestion every run.
doNotMerge.source: this map's own review (2026-07-25); Álvaro Lins is in the corpus's entity index

doNotMerge.reason: The corpus discusses both the SSPX archbishop and the Marxist philosopher; an ASR-driven merge on the surname would fuse a Catholic traditionalist with a French Marxist.
doNotMerge.source: perennialism/KEYWORDS.md - 'Lefebvre conflates Marcel (SSPX) with Henri (the Marxist philosopher) in COF; recorded on archive#13 §2'
